extracted.intended_audience: Researchers / authors submitting manuscripts to PLOS ONE
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting primary scientific research manuscripts to PLOS ONE, including scope, originality, technical standards, ethics, language, reporting, and data availability requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: The study presents the results of primary scientific research
rubrics_metrics.description: The study presents the results of primary scientific research. PLOS ONE is designed to communicate primary scientific research. We welcome submissions in any applied discipline that will contribute to the base of scientific knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal will not consider: Reviews; Case studies (contemporary or historical); Study protocols; Hypothesis or proposal papers; Letters, commentaries, or essays; Opinion pieces; Policy papers; Any other type of secondary literature; Monographs; Purely theoretical research (such as pure mathematics). Occasionally commissioned Collection Reviews or Overviews are accepted only if solicited. Accepted/considered article types (with conditions): Systematic reviews (only if methods ensure comprehensive and unbiased sampling of existing literature—see submission guidelines); submissions describing methods, software, databases, or other tools if they follow appropriate reporting guidelines; qualitative research only if it adheres to appropriate study design and reporting guidelines; studies reporting negative results. See submission guidelines for discipline-specific requirements and reporting guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results reported have not been published elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: Results reported have not been published elsewhere. PLOS ONE does not accept for publication studies that have already been published, in whole or in part, elsewhere in the peer-reviewed literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All figures included should be original and not previously published. Submissions currently under consideration at other journals will not be considered. Preprints: deposition to preprint servers (e.g., bioRxiv, arXiv) or publication as a thesis does not prevent consideration. Conference presentations are acceptable. Replication studies or studies very similar to previous work require a sound scientific rationale and clear referencing/discussion of existing literature; derivative submissions without adequate justification will likely be rejected. See PLOS preprint server policy for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments, statistics, and analyses performed to high technical standard and described in sufficient detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments, statistics, and other analyses are performed to a high technical standard and are described in sufficient detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiments must be conducted rigorously with appropriate controls and replication. Sample sizes should be large enough to produce robust results where applicable. Methods and reagents must be described in sufficient detail to allow another researcher to reproduce the experiments. Follow discipline-specific reporting guidelines as indicated in the submission guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions are presented appropriately and supported by the data
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions are presented in an appropriate fashion and are supported by the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data presented in the manuscript must support the conclusions drawn. Submissions will be rejected if interpretation of results is unjustified or inappropriate. Authors should avoid overstating conclusions. Authors may discuss possible implications but must clearly label such discussion as hypotheses rather than as definitive conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article presented intelligibly and written in standard English
rubrics_metrics.description: The article is presented in an intelligible fashion and is written in standard English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS ONE does not copyedit accepted manuscripts, so submitted language must be clear, correct, and unambiguous. The journal may reject papers that do not meet these standards. If language is difficult to understand or contains many errors, authors may be recommended to seek independent editorial or manuscript editing services prior to revising for resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research meets applicable standards for ethics of experimentation and research integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: The research meets all applicable standards for the ethics of experimentation and research integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS ONE reserves the right to reject submissions that do not meet ethical standards, which may be more stringent than local standards. Approval from the relevant ethics body is required for studies involving: humans (including observational/survey-based studies or any personal data), animals (including observational studies), non-commercial cell lines, field sampling, and studies with potential biosafety implications. If approval was not obtained, authors must explain why it was not required. For publication ethics, PLOS ONE is a member of COPE and expects compliance with best practices on authorship, dual publication, plagiarism, figure manipulation, and competing interests. Contact plosone@plos.org or see Editorial Policies and Submission Guidelines for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to reporting guidelines and community standards for data availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The article adheres to appropriate reporting guidelines and community standards for data availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results must be rigorously reported as appropriate to community standards; discipline-specific reporting guidelines are referenced in submission guidelines. Authors must follow standards and practices for data deposition in publicly available resources (e.g., gene sequence databases, microarray repositories, structural study databases). Failure to comply with community standards for data sharing and deposition may result in rejection. See the PLOS ONE data availability policy for detailed requirements.
